kitDescription: Quency: Escape Queen is a Water-element SMG Attacker (Burst III, 40s cooldown) who ramps herself up by firing. Her Skill 2 'Explore Route' fires every couple of normal attacks and builds three cumulative tiers of self stacks — ATK and Hit Rate together — where each higher tier only starts building once the tier below it is at max, so a sustained magazine takes her to roughly +110% ATK and +61 points of Hit Rate; the higher tiers use very short windows (1s and 0.5s) so they collapse during every reload and have to be rebuilt. Her Skill 1 'Secure Route' pays out three permanent self bonuses, each unlocked only while the matching Explore Route tier is sitting at max stacks: more Distributed Damage, more core damage, and more Critical Rate. Her burst 'The Great Thief' gives herself +57.08% Attack Damage and +25.87% Reload Speed for 10 seconds (the reload buff is a real damage lever on a 120-round magazine) and hits all enemies for 1736.31% of her final ATK as Distributed Damage. The Distributed Damage bonus from Skill 1 exists purely to amplify that burst nuke — it is the only distributed-flavored hit she has — so the two lines are one mechanic split across two skills.

skill1.driverSaid: passive self buff distributedDamagePct 49.58, no gate, no duration (expiresFrame null); note argues 'faithful IN EFFECT' because the only consumer (the nuke) first fires ~5.4s, long after the ~1s stage-1 build, and the 2s stage-1 window outlasts the 1.35s reload.
skill1.blindSaid: S6 blind: same stat/value as a passive but with rampSec 6 as an invented staircase stand-in for stage saturation (blind flags the staircase itself as ⚑). S5 blind pinned self-scope + load-bearing + flavor coupling and it/skipped the gate as a missing engine primitive. S2b (fable) would call a frame-0 apply RED on strict gate reading.
skill1.formulaCheck: distributedDamagePct routes to the Distributed bucket (damage-calculation §1g), which multiplies distributed-flavored instances ONLY — correct bucket, and the driver test reads mult.distributed 1.4958 on the nuke and 1.0000 on normals, so it neither leaks into Damage-Up nor touches normals. Prose magnitude exact.
skill1.explanation: The prose gate ('only when Explore Route Stage 1 is at max stacks') is not encoded; the engine has no at-max-stacks trigger, and the omission is documented with a recipe and tier (engine-primitive). The driver's 'zero observable effect' claim is CONDITIONAL, not proven: it holds only if the stage-1 pool is genuinely at max at every one of her cast instants. Stage-1's 2s window beats a 1.35s reload with only ~0.65s of margin, and a reload landing inside the ~1.5s burst chain would eat that margin — from the shipped event stream this is unobservable, so treat it as a hypothesis (the one same-model residual worth an owner spot-check). Direction of any error is a small over-credit on the nuke, never an under-credit.

skill1.driverSaid: hitCount 20 → self coreDamagePct 25.25, durationSec 1, maxStacks 1 — a firing-tracking proxy for the stage-2-max gate (continuous while firing, lapses ~1s into a reload).
skill1.blindSaid: S6 blind: passive coreDamagePct 25.25 + rampSec 10 (a coarser stand-in for the same gate). S5 blind pinned stat/value/self-scope and load-bearing, and it/skipped the gate.
skill1.formulaCheck: 'Damage dealt when attacking core' → coreDamagePct, which enters coreBonus inside the additive Major bracket (damage-calculation §1b) — correct bucket, and NOT the generic Damage-Up bucket a nearest-wrong encoding would use. Magnitude exact vs prose.
skill1.explanation: Proxy fires every 20 rounds; at the live SMG cadence (frame-quantized 20 pulls/s × hitsPerShot 2 = 40 rounds/s) that is one apply per 0.5s against a 1s window, so the buff is continuous while firing and lapses during a reload — a structurally sound stand-in for a gate that is itself continuous-while-firing. Residual: the hit counter carries across reloads, so the rebuild after firing resumes is slightly optimistic, and the opening ~1s is over-credited because the real gate cannot open until stage-1 has capped first. Both documented; magnitude, duration, self-target and liveness are pinned by test.

skill1.driverSaid: hitCount 10 → self critRatePct 16.73, durationSec 0.5, maxStacks 1 — same proxy construction, one tier tighter.
skill1.blindSaid: S6 blind: passive critRatePct 16.73 + rampSec 14. S5 blind additionally asserted that NO critRateNormalPct 16.73 apply exists (the over-scoping trap) — GREEN against the driver's override.
skill1.formulaCheck: Prose carries no 'of normal attacks' qualifier, so unscoped critRatePct is correct; critRateNormalPct would wrongly withhold the lift from skill/burst instances (game-mechanics §11). Crit enters the Major bracket as critRate × critBonus; the driver test shows the top resolved crit rates collapse 0.3173/0.4637 → 0.15/0.2964 when removed, so it is live on real damage instances.
skill1.explanation: Proxy fires every 10 rounds ≈ every 0.25s against a 0.5s window → continuous while firing. This also RESOLVES the S2b (fable) worry that stage-3 uptime is marginal: fable assumed the trigger fires once per two PULLS, but with hitsPerShot 2 it fires once per pull (~20/s), so 5 stacks of a 0.5s buff accrue in ~0.25s and saturation is comfortable rather than borderline. Gate timing remains approximate and documented.

skill2.driverSaid: hitCount 2 self block: hitRatePct 1.36, durationSec 2, maxStacks 10 (per-stack value, real engine stacking).
skill2.blindSaid: S6 blind PRE-SUMMED it to 13.6 with rampSec 6 — coarser, and the blind flags its own encoding as an upper bound. S5 blind pinned per-stack value, maxStacks 10 and near-cap saturation, which the driver's per-stack encoding satisfies and the blind's own pre-summed override would fail.
skill2.formulaCheck: hitRatePct is a live damage stat here: it feeds acrForHR / UNIGEO, shrinking the accuracy circle and lifting core rate (game-mechanics §7). Not droppable as accuracy flavor. Kit percentage is DATAMINED-exact; only the HR→core conversion slope is the engine's global ⚑, correctly left alone rather than re-fit per unit.
skill2.explanation: Driver's per-stack + maxStacks + durationSec encoding is strictly more faithful than the blind's pre-summed value: it reproduces real accrual, lapse and rebuild. Test pins maxStacks 10 and expiresFrame−frame = 120 frames structurally, and the hit-rate-only counterfactual (ATK kept) both drops her total and shifts the normal core-rate distribution — so the HR→core chain is demonstrably live, not decorative.

skill2.blindSaid: S6 blind pre-summed to 24.5 + rampSec. S5 blind pinned per-stack value + cap + saturation: GREEN.
skill2.formulaCheck: atkPct sums into (1 + Σ ATK%) on staticAtk (damage-calculation §1a) — the diluting bucket, correct for a plain 'ATK ▲ x%' line; not a caster-ATK flat grant.
skill2.explanation: Correct stat and stacking semantics; self-only (allies unmoved in both driver and blind counterfactuals). The three ATK tiers are authored as three distinct values, so the engine's same-(caster,slot,stat,value) dedupe keeps them as three co-stacking keys — which is exactly the cascade reading ('each subsequent effect triggers all effects before it' = additive, not replace).

skill2.driverSaid: hitRatePct 2.71, durationSec 1, maxStacks 10, in the SAME hitCount-2 block as stage 1 (no stage-1-max prerequisite encoded — documented ⚑2).
skill2.blindSaid: S6 blind pre-summed 27.1 + rampSec 10. S5 blind pinned value/cap and it/skipped the prerequisite as a missing primitive.
skill2.formulaCheck: Same HR→core routing as stage 1; the 1s window is shorter than the 81-frame (1.35s) reload, so the tier correctly collapses on every reload and must rebuild — which is what makes the shorter duration load-bearing rather than cosmetic.
skill2.explanation: Magnitude, cap and duration exact. The un-encoded stage-unlock ordering (stage 2 should only build while stage 1 is capped) is a documented ⚑ with an engine-primitive tier; its effect is confined to the ~1s opening ramp and ~0.4–0.8s after each post-reload rebuild, i.e. a small over-credit in transients only — steady state is unaffected.

skill2.blindSaid: S6 blind pre-summed 49.0. S5 blind pinned cap 10 (not 5, the stage-3 bleed trap) and the 1s window: GREEN.
skill2.formulaCheck: ATK% bucket, as stage 1. Prose phrasing wobble ('stacks up to 10 time(s)') carries the same semantics; driver read it correctly.
skill2.explanation: Cap correctly 10 here and 5 at stage 3 — the driver test asserts that asymmetry explicitly, so a flat-x10 mis-encoding of the ladder would fail.

skill2.blindSaid: S6 blind pre-summed 20.4 + rampSec 14. S5 blind pinned maxStacks 5 and 30-frame window: GREEN.
skill2.formulaCheck: HR→core routing again; cap drop to 5 and 0.5s window both match prose exactly.
skill2.explanation: At one activation per pull (~20/s) the 5-stack cap saturates in ~0.25s inside a 0.5s window, so this tier — and therefore skill1's crit gate that depends on it — holds while firing and lapses across reloads. Uptime is NOT asserted as 100% anywhere, consistent with fable's note (8).

skill2.blindSaid: S6 blind pre-summed 36.8. S5 blind required three CONCURRENT distinct atkPct keys with caps 10/10/5 — the driver's encoding is the only one of the two that satisfies it.
skill2.formulaCheck: Ceiling of the full ladder = +24.5 + 49.0 + 36.8 = +110.3% ATK inside the single (1+ΣATK%) sum, which is the correct additive-within-bucket behavior.
skill2.explanation: Three independent pools with distinct caps and decay order (3 → 2 → 1 across a reload) fall out of the encoding rather than being asserted by hand. Removing skill2 entirely more than halves her total, so the ladder is the dominant part of her kit and its structural pins are the highest-value assertions in the file.

burst.driverSaid: burstCast → self attackDamagePct 57.08, durationSec 10; test asserts once per HER cast (distinct apply frames == her burstCast count) and a 600-frame window.
burst.blindSaid: Identical encoding (burstCast, not fullBurstEnter) and the blind independently bounded the window by showing 1s is worse and 30s is better than shipped — so the duration is real, not permanent.
burst.formulaCheck: attackDamagePct enters the Damage-Up bucket (damage-calculation §1e), multiplying against the ATK% bucket rather than summing with it — correct placement.
burst.explanation: burstCast keying is the load-bearing discrimination in this fixture: helm is a co-Burst-III, so a fullBurstEnter mis-key would over-credit rotations she does not cast, and the apply-frames == her-casts assertion fails under it. Both blind agents converge on burstCast.

burst.driverSaid: burstCast → self reloadSpeedPct 25.87, durationSec 10, in the same block; note explicitly treats reload speed as a damage lever (shot count).
burst.blindSaid: Same encoding, and the S5 blind supplied the counterfactual the driver test lacks: zeroing reloadSpeedPct strictly reduces her total — GREEN against the shipped override.
burst.formulaCheck: Reload is subtractive (displayed × 0.975 × (1−buff) + 13f, game-mechanics §2), so on an 81-frame reload the buff buys real rounds inside the window. Not a defensive/QoL line.
burst.explanation: Faithful and demonstrated load-bearing — but note WHERE: the driver's own test only pins magnitude, 10s duration and once-per-cast; the proof that the line moves damage comes from the S5 blind run, which passed against the shipped override. Coverage is met (an existing labeled check exists and is green); a future edit to the driver test should keep or absorb that counterfactual so the line cannot silently rot into an inert stat.

burst.driverSaid: burstCast → enemy flatDamage atkPct 1736.31, flavor 'distributed', no explicit noFb/crit (relies on engine defaults); test pins one hit per cast, atkPct 1736.31, mult.distributed 1.4958, fbMajorApplied false, and that stripping the flavor collapses it to 1.0000.
burst.blindSaid: S6 blind identical but with explicit noFb:true and crit:true. Behaviorally equivalent on the FB side (burst-cast damage is FB-exempt by engine ordering); the crit side is an unstated default in the driver's file.
burst.formulaCheck: Distributed instances take their own Distributed bucket and deal full total against one target — no split penalty on the partless boss (damage-calculation §1g). FB-exemption matches the MEASURED burst-cast boundary rule (§1b): cast damage lands before the window opens, so no +50%. Magnitude exact vs prose.
burst.explanation: This is the strongest pair of assertions in the gauntlet: the nuke and skill1's 49.58% are two halves of one mechanic, and the driver proves the coupling in both directions (removing the buff and stripping the flavor produce the same collapse to mult.distributed 1.0000), which kills both nearest-wrongs — a generic Damage-Up encoding of the buff and an unflavored nuke that would leave skill1 silently inert. One undocumented reliance: crit eligibility on a distributed hit (see gotcha 1).

gotchas.summary: The nuke's crit eligibility rides an engine default on a bucket the SSOT itself marks as disputed, and the override never says so.
gotchas.evidence: Kit line 'Deals 1736.31% of final ATK as Distributed Damage' says nothing about crit. The driver's flatDamage carries no crit field, so it takes the function-damage default (crit at the caster's rate, damage-calculation §2b); the S6 blind wrote crit:true explicitly, reaching the same behavior. But damage-calculation §1's per-type table lists crit for DISTRIBUTED damage as '⚠️ disputed' (as it does full-burst and element for that row). Neither the note nor the caveats flags this, and her S1 crit line (+16.73) plus her sheet crit make it a material share of a ~17× multiplier hit.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Add a caveat recording that the nuke inherits the engine's crit-on default for distributed damage while the SSOT marks distributed-crit disputed — do not change the number. Measurement recipe: on a focus recording of her burst, read the nuke popup colour/icon across several casts (orange + icon = crit-eligible, white-only across many casts = crit-exempt); a crit/non-crit popup PAIR at ×1.5 settles it outright. This is an engine-global convention question, so resolve it once for all distributed carriers rather than per unit.

gotchas.summary: The override note's cadence premise (24 pulls/s) contradicts the live engine default of 20 pulls/s for SMG.
gotchas.evidence: Note/caveat: 'cadence = datamined 24 pulls/s (SHOT rate = rate_of_fire 1440rpm/60)' and '⚑1 MANDATORY cadence tuple: pullsPerSec 24'. game-mechanics §2 records SMG frame quantization as DEFAULT-ON since 2026-07-23 (1440rpm = 2.5 frames → ceil 3 frames = 20.0/s, MEASURED by ammo-counter read; SMGRATE=24 is the documented revert arm only). So the note describes the reverted arm as if it were live, and the derived timings in the note ('every 20 hits ≈ 0.42s', '48 bullets/s') are computed off the wrong rate.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Correct the note to 20 effective pulls/s (40 rounds/s at hitsPerShot 2), citing the frame-quantization rule, and restate the proxy arithmetic: hitCount 20 → one apply per 0.5s vs a 1s window, hitCount 10 → per 0.25s vs 0.5s, hitCount 2 → ~20 applies/s. No override value or assertion changes: I re-derived every proxy and stack window at 20/s and all of them still saturate and still lapse only across reloads, so the encoding is cadence-robust — this is a documentation correction, not a model change.

verdictRationale: All 12 kit lines are FAITHFUL or DOCUMENTED_GAP (9 / 3), and the mechanical convergence check is clean: the S5 blind test file, written from prose alone, runs GREEN against the driver's SHIPPED override (16 passed, 5 honest it.skips, zero RED) with only an import-path adaptation — so the strongest available evidence, an independent derivation failing to contradict the implementation, points to GO. The three DOCUMENTED_GAPs are all the same missing engine primitive: the kit's 'Explore Route Stage N at max stacks' gates have no at-max-stacks trigger to encode, so skill1's lines are firing-tracking proxies (passive / hitCount 20 with a 1s window / hitCount 10 with a 0.5s window) and skill2's stage-unlock ordering builds in parallel. Both blind agents hit the identical wall and both flagged it, which is corroboration that the gap is real rather than driver laziness; the driver's proxies are also strictly better than the S6 blind's invented rampSec 6/10/14 staircase, and its per-stack skill2 encoding (values 1.36/2.45/2.71/4.9/4.08/7.36 with caps 10/10/5 and windows 2s/1s/0.5s) is materially more faithful than the blind's pre-summed max-stack values, which the blind itself labelled an upper-bound over-credit. Error direction of every gap is a small over-credit confined to the opening ramp and post-reload rebuilds. Discrimination holds: every load-bearing line is pinned structurally off buffApply (stat, value, maxStacks, expiresFrame−frame) so a wrong stat, cap or duration fails, and the two traps that actually matter are killed outright — a generic attackDamagePct encoding of the 49.58% would lift her normals (shipped model provably does not) and an unflavored nuke would leave skill1 silently inert (both counterfactuals collapse mult.distributed to 1.0000). One coverage note rather than a defect: the proof that Reload Speed is load-bearing lives in the S5 blind run, not the driver's own test. Two low-severity findings, neither blocking: the nuke's crit eligibility relies on an engine default for a bucket the SSOT marks disputed and is undocumented, and the note's 24-pulls/s cadence premise is stale against the live 20/s SMG frame quantization (I re-derived every proxy and stack window at 20/s — all still saturate, so no value changes). Same-model residual for the owner to spot-check: the driver's claim that the passive-encoded 49.58% has ZERO observable error is conditional, not proven — it requires the stage-1 pool to be at max at every cast instant, and its 2s window clears a 1.35s reload by only ~0.65s, a margin a reload landing inside the ~1.5s burst chain could erase. Fable's separate worry that stage-3 uptime is marginal is RESOLVED in the driver's favour: with hitsPerShot 2 the trigger fires once per pull, not once per two pulls, so 5 stacks accrue in ~0.25s inside a 0.5s window.
